title: auto_scaling_and_elastic_load_balancers
topic: Auto Scaling and Elastic Load Balancer

questions.question: Which of the following are required elements of an Auto Scaling group?

explanation.summary: Desired capacity defines the target number of EC2 instances in the group.
explanation.why: An Auto Scaling group uses desired capacity to determine how many instances should be running under normal conditions.

explanation.summary: Minimum size ensures a baseline number of instances remain running.
explanation.why: Auto Scaling groups require a minimum instance count to maintain availability even during scaling activities.
explanation.comparison: Minimum size prevents scaling below a defined threshold.

explanation.summary: Launch configurations define how instances are launched but are not group sizing parameters.
explanation.why: Launch configurations are associated with the Auto Scaling group, but the question focuses on required group elements related to capacity settings.

explanation.summary: Health checks monitor instance status but are not core sizing elements.
explanation.why: Health checks help determine whether instances should be replaced, but they are not considered required capacity elements of the group itself.

questions.question: Which of the following are the minimum required elements to create an Auto Scaling launch configuration?

options.text: Launch configuration name, AMI, instance type, and key pair

explanation.summary: Key pairs are optional for launch configurations.
explanation.why: A key pair can be added for SSH access but is not mandatory when creating a launch configuration.

options.text: Launch configuration name, Amazon Machine Image (AMI), and instance type

explanation.summary: A launch configuration minimally requires a name, AMI, and instance type.
explanation.why: These parameters define the template for launching EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group.

options.text: Launch configuration name, AMI, instance type, key pair, security group, and block device mapping

explanation.summary: Several listed parameters are optional rather than minimum requirements.
explanation.why: Security groups, block device mappings, and key pairs may be configured but are not mandatory for the minimum configuration.

options.text: Launch configuration name, AMI, instance type, key pair, and security group

explanation.summary: Key pairs and security groups are optional additions.
explanation.why: The minimum required launch configuration only requires a name, AMI, and instance type.

questions.question: Which of the following must be configured on an Elastic Load Balancing load balancer to accept incoming traffic?

explanation.summary: Network interfaces are managed automatically by AWS.
explanation.why: Elastic Load Balancing abstracts networking components and does not require manual interface configuration.

explanation.summary: Ports are configured within listeners rather than independently.
explanation.why: A listener defines both the protocol and port for incoming traffic.

explanation.summary: Instances are registered targets rather than listener configurations.
explanation.why: Load balancers distribute traffic to instances but do not require a specific instance to accept traffic.

explanation.summary: Listeners define how the load balancer accepts incoming traffic.
explanation.why: A listener checks for incoming connection requests using a configured protocol and port and routes requests to targets.

questions.question: If an instance fails Elastic Load Balancing health checks, which statement is true?

options.text: The instance is quarantined by the load balancer for root cause analysis

explanation.summary: Elastic Load Balancing does not quarantine failed instances.
explanation.why: The load balancer simply marks unhealthy targets and stops routing traffic to them.

options.text: The instance is replaced automatically by the load balancer.

explanation.summary: Replacement is handled by Auto Scaling rather than the load balancer.
explanation.why: Elastic Load Balancing only routes traffic and performs health checks.
explanation.comparison: Auto Scaling replaces unhealthy instances, while ELB routes traffic.

options.text: The instance is terminated automatically by the load balancer.

explanation.summary: Elastic Load Balancing does not terminate EC2 instances.
explanation.why: Termination actions are outside the scope of the load balancer service.

options.text: The load balancer stops sending traffic to the instance that failed its health check.

explanation.summary: Unhealthy instances are removed from traffic routing.
explanation.why: When a target fails health checks, the load balancer stops routing requests to it until it becomes healthy again.
keyPoints: Routes traffic only to healthy targets

questions.question: Which deployment provides high availability across three Availability Zones while maintaining at least 65 percent capacity?

options.text: Deploy the application on three servers in ap-northeast-1a, three servers in ap-northeast-1b, and three servers in ap-northeast-1c.

explanation.summary: Distributing instances evenly across Availability Zones improves high availability.
explanation.why: With nine instances distributed equally across three AZs, losing one AZ still leaves six running instances, which is approximately 66 percent capacity.

options.text: Deploy the application on four servers in ap-northeast-1a and five servers in apnortheast-1b, and keep five stopped instances in ap-northeast-1a as reserve.

explanation.summary: Stopped reserve instances do not provide immediate high availability.
explanation.why: Stopped instances require startup time and do not satisfy active multi-AZ redundancy requirements.

options.text: Deploy the application on six servers in ap-northeast-1b and three servers in apnortheast-1c.

explanation.summary: Using only two Availability Zones reduces resilience.
explanation.why: Failure of the larger AZ would reduce capacity below the required threshold.

options.text: Deploy the application on nine servers in ap-northeast-1b, and keep nine stopped instances in ap-northeast-1a as reserve.

explanation.summary: Single-AZ deployments create a single point of failure.
explanation.why: If the AZ fails, all active instances become unavailable.

questions.question: Which of the following are characteristics of the Auto Scaling service on AWS?

options.text: Responds to changing conditions by adding or terminating Amazon EC2 instances

explanation.summary: Auto Scaling dynamically adjusts instance count based on demand.
explanation.why: The service automatically launches or terminates instances according to scaling policies and metrics.

options.text: Enforces a minimum number of running Amazon EC2 instances

explanation.summary: Auto Scaling maintains a minimum healthy capacity.
explanation.why: Minimum size settings ensure that the required baseline number of instances is always available.

options.text: Launches instances from a specified Amazon Machine Image (AMI)

explanation.summary: Auto Scaling uses AMIs to create EC2 instances consistently.
explanation.why: Launch configurations and launch templates specify the AMI used for new instances.
examples: Launching web servers from a standard image

options.text: Sends traffic to only healthy instances

explanation.summary: Traffic routing is handled by Elastic Load Balancing.
explanation.why: Auto Scaling manages instance count, while load balancers distribute traffic to healthy targets.
explanation.comparison: Auto Scaling scales resources, ELB routes traffic.

questions.question: An Auto Scaling group may use:

explanation.summary: Auto Scaling groups support On-Demand EC2 instances.
explanation.why: On-Demand Instances can be launched and terminated automatically based on scaling policies.

explanation.summary: Auto Scaling groups support Spot Instances for cost optimization.
explanation.why: Spot Instances can reduce compute costs and can be combined with On-Demand capacity.
explanation.performanceImpact: Spot interruptions may occur when AWS reclaims capacity.

explanation.summary: Terminated instances cannot participate in Auto Scaling groups.
explanation.why: Only active or launchable instances are managed by the group.

options.text: Already running instances if they use the same Amazon Machine Image (AMI) as the Auto Scaling group's launch configuration and are not already part of another Auto Scaling group

explanation.summary: Existing instances are not required to match the same AMI to attach to a group.
explanation.why: Instances can be attached to an Auto Scaling group without requiring the same AMI.

learnMore.title: Attach EC2 Instances to Auto Scaling Groups

questions.question: Elastic Load Balancing supports which types of load balancers?

explanation.summary: Internet-facing load balancers route requests from the public internet.
explanation.why: These load balancers have public IP addresses and distribute external traffic to targets.

explanation.summary: Extranet is not an Elastic Load Balancing deployment type.
explanation.why: AWS categorizes ELBs as internet-facing or internal.

explanation.summary: WWW is not a recognized ELB type.
explanation.why: Load balancers are categorized by accessibility and architecture rather than web terminology.

explanation.summary: Internal load balancers distribute traffic within private networks.
explanation.why: Internal ELBs route traffic only inside a VPC and are commonly used for internal applications.

questions.question: Auto Scaling groups always remain the same size.

explanation.summary: Auto Scaling groups dynamically adjust capacity based on demand.
explanation.why: Scaling policies allow the group size to increase or decrease automatically.

explanation.summary: Auto Scaling groups can grow or shrink automatically.
explanation.why: The service adjusts instance counts according to scaling metrics, schedules, or policies.
keyPoints: Supports scale out and scale in

questions.question: Elastic Load Balancers are only good for balancing the load.

explanation.summary: Elastic Load Balancers provide additional capabilities beyond traffic distribution.
explanation.why: ELBs also perform health checks, SSL termination, failover support, and integration with Auto Scaling.

explanation.summary: Elastic Load Balancers support monitoring, health checks, and fault tolerance.
explanation.why: In addition to balancing traffic, ELBs improve application availability and resilience.

questions.question: Elastic load balancers only exist in one AZ.

explanation.summary: Elastic Load Balancers can span multiple Availability Zones.
explanation.why: ELBs are designed for high availability and can distribute traffic across multiple AZs.

explanation.summary: Elastic Load Balancers support multi-AZ deployments.
explanation.why: AWS recommends enabling multiple Availability Zones for improved fault tolerance.
examples: Application Load Balancer across three AZs

questions.question: Question 12 was not visible in the provided images.
Which of the below is true about the Network Load Balancer?

explanation.summary: Network Load Balancers provide static IP addresses.
explanation.why: NLBs can be associated with Elastic IP addresses, making them suitable for fixed-address requirements.

explanation.summary: Network Load Balancers operate at Layer 4 of the OSI model.
explanation.why: NLBs route TCP, UDP, and TLS traffic rather than presentation-layer traffic.

explanation.summary: Network Load Balancers preserve source IP information.
explanation.why: NLBs maintain low latency and preserve packet headers while forwarding traffic.
explanation.comparison: Unlike some proxies, NLBs preserve original client source IPs.

options.text: Best Support for High Traffic Sites

explanation.summary: Network Load Balancers are optimized for extremely high performance workloads.
explanation.why: NLBs are designed to handle millions of requests per second with ultra-low latency.
explanation.performanceImpact: Suitable for high-throughput TCP and UDP applications.

questions.question: A single Elastic Load Balancer can have multiple listeners?

explanation.summary: Elastic Load Balancers can use multiple listeners for different protocols and ports.
explanation.why: A load balancer may have separate listeners for HTTP, HTTPS, TCP, or other supported protocols.

explanation.summary: Load balancers support multiple listener configurations.
explanation.why: Listeners can be added to support multiple application protocols and ports simultaneously.

explanation.summary: Elastic Load Balancers incur AWS usage charges.
explanation.why: AWS bills load balancers based on uptime and processed traffic.

explanation.summary: Elastic Load Balancers are billed services in AWS.
explanation.why: Charges apply for load balancer hours and data processing usage.
explanation.comparison: ELB pricing varies depending on load balancer type and traffic volume.
